title: Edge-Orientation Entropy Predicts Preference for Diverse Types of Man-Made Images
research_questions: Does edge-orientation entropy predict aesthetic ratings in a wide variety of man-made visual patterns and scenes?
How does edge-orientation entropy relate to the well-established human preference for curved over angular shapes?
Do edge-orientation entropy and curvilinearity share predicted variance of preference for visual stimuli?
hypotheses: Edge orientation entropy is a predictor for aesthetic ratings in at least some man-made visual stimuli.
Human observers prefer a high degree of edge-orientation entropy in more complex visual stimuli, including photographs of man-made objects and scenes.
Edge-orientation entropy and curvilinearity share predicted variance of preference for visual stimuli.

methodology.participants: 18-31 participants per experiment (university students or graduates, <40 years old, normal/corrected-to-normal vision, no art professionals).
methodology.stimuli: Five sets of man-made images: (1) Simple irregular geometric shapes (curved/angular, N=3600); (2) Artificial ornamental patterns (Taprats, N=100); (3) Photographs of building facades (N=50); (4) Interior architectural scenes (N=200); (5) Music album covers (classic, pop, metal, N=150); (6) Complex artificial line patterns (angular/curved, N=100) with systematically varied 2nd-order edge-orientation entropy.
methodology.procedure: Participants rated images on a 0-100 continuous scale (converted to 0-1) for 'pleasing', 'interesting', and 'harmonious' (except Exp 1 & 4 which used existing preference/beauty ratings). Stimuli presented on a black screen (EIZO ColorEdge CG241W) at 70 cm viewing distance (135x135mm). Order of subjective categories and images randomized.

objective_image_properties: 1st-order edge-orientation entropy (Shannon entropy of summary orientation histogram, 24 Gabor filters, max 4.585)
2nd-order edge-orientation entropy (Shannon entropy of pairwise edge orientation comparisons, 24 Gabor filters, max 4.585, distance ranges 20-240 pixels and >240 pixels)
Edge density (sum of Gabor filter responses)
Self-similarity (PHOG descriptor method, mean value for pyramid levels 1-3)
Architectural features (binary: openness, ceiling height, contour)

methodology.analysis: Multiple linear regression (lm package in R) to predict ratings from image properties. Models included: Full model (Model 1), Entropies only (Model 2), Entropies + Shape (Model 3), Shape alone (Model 4). R2adj, AIC, standardized regression coefficients (βi) reported. ANOVA (R2 difference test) for model comparison. Mann-Whitney U test for entropy differences between shape types.

findings.mechanism: Curved shapes are generally preferred over angular shapes, a well-established phenomenon in aesthetics.
A more uniform distribution of edge orientations is associated with higher aesthetic preference.
A higher independence of edge orientations across an image is associated with higher aesthetic preference.
Curved patterns inherently contain a more uniform distribution of edge orientations compared to angular patterns dominated by specific straight line orientations.
findings.source: Experiment 1: Patterns by Bertamini et al. (2016) - Discussion
findings.quote: First-order entropy was higher for the curved stimuli (median: 4.47) than for the angular ones (median: 4.35; Mann-Whitney test, U = 80, p < 0.0001).

findings.mechanism: Curved patterns inherently contain more independent edge orientations compared to angular patterns.
findings.source: Experiment 1: Patterns by Bertamini et al. (2016) - Discussion
findings.quote: A similar relation was obtained for 2nd-order entropy (median: 4.26 and 4.15, respectively; U = 674, p = 0.0001).

findings.mechanism: Edge-orientation entropies capture underlying visual properties that drive preference, performing comparably to explicit shape classification.
findings.source: Experiment 1: Patterns by Bertamini et al. (2016) - Discussion
findings.quote: our findings suggest that the two measures of entropy together predict the preference ratings of the stimuli about as well as their curved/angular shape

findings.mechanism: Higher independence of edge orientations contributes to perceived pleasingness in complex ornamental patterns.
Lower self-similarity contributes to perceived pleasingness in complex ornamental patterns.
Higher independence of edge orientations contributes to perceived interestingness in complex ornamental patterns.
Lower self-similarity contributes to perceived interestingness in complex ornamental patterns.
A more uniform distribution of edge orientations contributes to perceived harmoniousness in complex ornamental patterns.
Less independent edge orientations (more regularity) contributes to perceived harmoniousness in complex ornamental patterns.
Higher self-similarity contributes to perceived harmoniousness in complex ornamental patterns.
More evenly distributed edge orientations, possibly achieved by complementing cardinal orientations with oblique elements, increase pleasingness in building facades.
More evenly distributed edge orientations increase interestingness in building facades.
More evenly distributed edge orientations increase harmoniousness in building facades.
A more irregular spatial distribution of edge orientations (higher 2nd-order entropy) increases harmoniousness in building facades.
Openness is a strong predictor of pleasantness in interior architectural scenes, potentially related to approach/avoidance responses.
Higher edge density contributes to perceived pleasantness in interior architectural scenes.
Lower self-similarity contributes to perceived pleasantness in interior architectural scenes.
Openness is a strong predictor of beauty in interior architectural scenes, potentially related to approach/avoidance responses.
Higher edge density contributes to perceived beauty in interior architectural scenes.
Lower self-similarity contributes to perceived beauty in interior architectural scenes.
In interior architectural scenes, other factors like openness, edge density, and self-similarity are stronger predictors of pleasantness than contour.
In interior architectural scenes, other factors like openness, edge density, and self-similarity are stronger predictors of beauty than contour.
A more uniform distribution of edge orientations contributes to perceived pleasingness in music album covers.
Less independent edge orientations (more regularity) contributes to perceived pleasingness in music album covers.
Metal music covers often feature exciting, shocking, or disgusting content that strongly arouses observer interest, overriding formal image properties.
A more uniform distribution of edge orientations contributes to perceived harmoniousness in music album covers.
Less independent edge orientations (more regularity) contributes to perceived harmoniousness in music album covers.

In complex, texture-like line patterns, angular shapes were rated more pleasing than curved shapes, suggesting that overall edge statistics (entropy) can override the preference for individual line curvature.
Lower independence of edge orientations at shorter distances contributes to pleasingness in complex line patterns.
Higher independence of edge orientations at longer distances contributes to pleasingness in complex line patterns.
Higher edge density contributes to perceived pleasingness in complex line patterns.
Higher self-similarity contributes to perceived pleasingness in complex line patterns.

In complex, texture-like line patterns, angular shapes were rated more interesting than curved shapes, suggesting that overall edge statistics (entropy) can override the preference for individual line curvature.
Lower independence of edge orientations at shorter distances contributes to interestingness in complex line patterns.
Higher independence of edge orientations at longer distances contributes to interestingness in complex line patterns.
Higher edge density contributes to perceived interestingness in complex line patterns.
Higher independence of edge orientations at longer distances contributes to harmoniousness in complex line patterns.
Higher edge density contributes to perceived harmoniousness in complex line patterns.
Higher self-similarity contributes to perceived harmoniousness in complex line patterns.
Edge-orientation entropies are powerful predictors of aesthetic ratings, sometimes surpassing or matching curvilinearity, by capturing fundamental visual statistics.
findings.source: Experiment 6: Angular/Curved Line Patterns - Discussion, General Discussion
findings.quote: Experiment 6 indicates that the edge-orientation entropies are more powerful predictors for ratings of pleasing and harmonious than curvilinearity.

findings.mechanism: Edge-orientation entropies can partly operationalize or substitute for curvilinearity in predicting aesthetic ratings, suggesting an underlying shared visual feature space that influences preference.
findings.quote: the edge-orientation entropies share a large portion of predicted variance for the preference for curved over angular stimuli. In other words, for most of the ratings in Experiments 1, 4, and 6, the entropies can substitute for the curvilinearity variable (shape or contour), at least in part, to predict the aesthetic ratings.

limitations: Study conducted in a laboratory setting.
Analysis restricted to six special types of man-made images, limiting generalizability.
Participants were undergraduates or had finished higher education, all younger than 40 years, potentially influencing ratings.
Idiosyncratic taste associated with cultural content (interior scenes, music album covers) may have affected ratings.
The study did not address inter-individual differences in aesthetic ratings.
